title: Postal Code Centroid Calculator: Center of Codes
description: Calculate an equal-weight spherical vector mean from up to 25 resolved postal codes. Results depend on external geocoding coverage.
summary_sentence: Resolve up to 25 postal codes and calculate an equal-weight spherical vector mean of the locations that are found.
quick_answer: The tool geocodes up to 25 postal codes and calculates the spherical vector mean of the resolved locations, with a distance for each. It does not necessarily minimise the average distance or travel time.

A geographic mean can suggest an initial search area. It does not guarantee a venue that minimises travel or average distance.
A list claiming to be 'Denver area' whose centroid lands in Kansas has a data problem. The centre is an audit with one number.
Resolve the supplied codes and review their returned locations before relying on their vector mean. Different geocoding providers can return different approximate points.

examples.label: Example · Why not average the latitudes?

body.t: Flat averaging of lat/lon distorts near the poles and the date line. This calculator averages directions on the sphere (the 3D vector method), then converts back — the difference is small for one county, real for one continent.

faq: How is the centre computed?
It is the normalised average of the resolved locations as 3D unit vectors, converted back to latitude and longitude. This is not generally the point that minimises average surface distance.
Which countries work?
ZIP and postal systems the resolver covers — US ZIPs are the home case; many other countries' postal codes resolve too, with coverage following the underlying open data.
Can I use the tool without sharing my precise location?
The tool does not request device location. Entered postal codes are sent to external geocoding providers and the calculated centre is reverse geocoded.
Why might a boundary or place name look different elsewhere?
Postal centroid datasets differ by source and vintage; another resolver's point for the same code can sit a little apart, nudging the centre.
Does MapBench store my browser location?
The tool does not request browser location. Postal codes and the calculated centre are sent to external geocoding services for lookup.
One code dominates my list — can I weight?
The centroid treats codes equally; repeat a code to weight it, or trim the list. The distances table shows each code's pull honestly.
The centre is in a lake or nowhere.
The mean can fall somewhere impractical. A reverse-geocoded place name is only a nearby label, not a verified venue.
Duplicate codes?
Fine — duplicates act as votes, which is sometimes exactly what attendance weighting should do.
Codes that fail to resolve?
They are reported rather than silently dropped, so your list's coverage is visible — check formats and country assumptions first.
Can I exclude outliers?
Trim the list and rerun — the centre's shift between runs is itself the outlier's measured pull. Deliberate, visible, honest.
Thousands of codes?
The tool accepts at most 25 codes per calculation. Larger datasets require a suitable GIS or batch workflow.
